key_insight: Augment curiosity-driven exploration with episodic context and a persistent world representation so agents remember where they’ve been across time, reducing revisits and escaping local loops in photorealistic 3D environments.
problem_solved: Agents driven by intrinsic curiosity often get stuck repeatedly revisiting previously 'forgotten' states in complex, realistic 3D worlds; this paper tackles how to maintain meaningful novelty signals over long horizons and across episodes.
method: Introduce episodic context that conditions intrinsic rewards on recent visitation, discouraging within-episode loops.
Maintain a persistent world representation across episodes so novelty is computed relative to long-term experience, not just the current episode.
Combine the above with a predictive model-based curiosity signal so the agent prioritizes truly novel and informative states in photorealistic 3D environments.
impact: Provides a practical way to scale curiosity-driven RL to realistic 3D tasks by preserving long-term memory of explored areas, improving sample efficiency and exploration quality for agents in simulation and embodied applications.

paper_title: Remember to be Curious: Episodic Context and Persistent Worlds for 3D Exploration
paper_authors: Lily Goli, Justin Kerr, Daniele Reda, Alec Jacobson, Andrea Tagliasacchi
